newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti says Telemedia issue is in budget.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti says Telemedia issue is in budget.

text.p: Italian information technology group Olivetti said a capital restructuring of its Telemedia company was already included in the group's budget and was aimed at consolidating the company's activities.
Earlier, a newspaper report said Telemedia, which contains the fixed line telecoms and media interests of Olivetti, had shown a loss of over 50 billion lire in 1996.

An Olivetti spokesman said that Telemedia contained businesses in start-up phases and therefore it was normal for it not to show a profit. But he declined to comment on the 50 billion lire loss figure.
Olivetti's full 1996 profit figures are due to be released on April 15 after a group board meeting.

Telemedia includes Olivetti's 67-percent owned joint venture Infostrada, with U.S. group Bell Atlantic holding the remaining 33 percent. Olivetti and France Telecom earlier this month signed a joint venture deal under which the French group would acquire 49 percent of Infostrada by subscribing to a 165 billion lire capital increase.
